edit.description: the async door every gate, runner operation and restore spawn reaches, whose child is handed a live stdin pipe nobody ends
its own capturing spawn, where a credential prompt is the same hang
the async capture beside the sync one, which already closes stdin and says why
the per-site verdict, which reads a declared cap and not a declared stdin
the detector's own domain and the shipped-tree absence verdict

summary: every spawn home ends its child's stdin, so a tool that falls back to reading it fails instead of holding a slot silently
acceptance: every capturing spawn home the shipped-tree scan names ends its child's stdin, and the scan's per-site verdict reports a home that declares its cap without it — so a child that reads stdin when nothing will write ends rather than waiting
tests: a capturing spawn home ends the stdin it opened for its child
a spawn home declaring its cap and not its stdin is a finding
pins: the sync capture door still ends its child's stdin
notes: Field instance: a `shell` gate running `prettier --check` with an empty file list fell back to stdin and held two build slots ~7h with no log line. `execFile` gives the child a stdin pipe (a socketpair on linux) nothing ends; `captureSync` already closes it and states why — one decision, two answers between the halves of one mechanism. Operator ruling: mechanism, no knob.
